subject: german
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.explain: 'Die Lunge' means 'the lung'; 'die Leber' is the liver.

questions.q: How do you say 'I do sport to keep fit'?
options: Ich treibe Sport, um fit zu bleiben
Er treibt Sport, um fit zu bleiben
Ich treibe Sport, weil ich fit bin
Ich treibe Sport, um dick zu werden
questions.explain: 'Sport treiben' = 'to do sport' and 'um... fit zu bleiben' = 'in order to keep fit'; 'ich treibe' is the correct form.

questions.q: What does 'Ich wohne am Stadtrand' mean?
options: I live on the outskirts of town
I live in the city centre
questions.explain: 'Der Stadtrand' means 'the edge/outskirts of the town', so 'Ich wohne am Stadtrand' = 'I live on the outskirts'.
'Die Spritze' means 'an injection/jab'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'I have to revise for my exams'?
options: Ich habe Lust auf meine Prüfungen
Ich muss für meine Prüfungen lernen
questions.explain: 'Lernen' here means 'to study/revise' and 'müssen' = 'to have to', so this means 'I have to revise for my exams'.

questions.q: What does 'das Viertel' mean (in a town)?
questions.explain: 'Das Viertel' means 'the neighbourhood/district' of a town (also 'a quarter' in time).
'Die Einwohner' means 'the inhabitants/residents' of a place.
'Die Ganztagsschule' means 'an all-day school' (with afternoon lessons too).
'Der Nachbar' means 'the neighbour' (female: 'die Nachbarin').
'Die Fußgängerzone' is the 'pedestrian zone/precinct' (from 'Fußgänger' = pedestrian).
'Das Rathaus' means 'the town hall' (from 'Rat' = council), not anything to do with rats.

questions.q: How do you say 'You should drink enough water'?
questions.explain: 'Genug' = 'enough' and 'trinken' = 'to drink'; 'wenig' (little) is the trap.
'Das Fach' means 'a (school) subject', e.g. 'mein Lieblingsfach' = 'my favourite subject'.
'Gesund' means 'healthy', so 'gesund leben' = 'to live healthily'.

questions.q: What does 'ausgewogen' mean (e.g. of a diet)?
questions.explain: 'Ausgewogen' means 'balanced', as in 'eine ausgewogene Ernährung' = 'a balanced diet'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'School starts at quarter past eight'?
options: Die Schule beginnt um halb acht
Die Schule endet um Viertel nach acht
Die Schule beginnt um Viertel nach acht
Die Schule beginnt um Viertel vor acht
questions.explain: 'Viertel nach acht' = 'quarter past eight'; 'vor' (to) is the distractor.

questions.q: What does 'die Pause' mean at school?
questions.explain: 'Die Pause' means 'the break/breaktime' between lessons.

questions.q: How do you say 'There is a swimming pool in my town'?
options: In meiner Stadt gibt es ein Rathaus
In meiner Stadt gibt es einen Bahnhof
In meiner Stadt gibt es ein Schwimmbad
In meiner Stadt fehlt ein Schwimmbad
questions.explain: 'Es gibt' = 'there is' and 'das Schwimmbad' = 'the swimming pool'.
'Das Zeugnis' means 'the (school) report/report card'.
'Die Metzgerei' (also 'Fleischerei') means 'the butcher's shop'.
'Gesund' means 'healthy'; the opposite is 'ungesund' (unhealthy).

questions.q: Which sentence means 'I have lived here for ten years'?
options: Ich wohnte vor zehn Jahren hier
Ich wohne seit zehn Jahren hier
Ich werde hier zehn Jahre wohnen
Ich wohne hier seit zehn Tagen
questions.explain: 'Seit' + present tense = 'for/since'; 'seit zehn Jahren' = 'for ten years'.
